pr.title: Skip cleanups on unsupported targets
pr.description:
This commit is an update to the `AbortUnwindingCalls` MIR pass in the compiler. Specifically a new boolean is added for "can this target possibly unwind" and if that's `false` then terminators are all adjusted to be unreachable/not present. The end result is that this fixes rust-lang/rust#140293 for wasm targets.

The motivation for this PR is that currently on WebAssembly targets the usage of the `C-unwind` ABI can lead LLVM to either (a) emit exception-handling instructions or (b) hit a LLVM-ICE-style codegen error. WebAssembly as a base instruction set does not support unwinding at all, and a later proposal to WebAssembly, the exception-handling proposal, was what enabled this. This means that the current intent of WebAssembly targets is that they maintain the baseline of "don't emit exception-handling instructions unless enabled". The commit here is intended to restore this behavior by skipping these instructions even when `C-unwind` is present.

Exception-handling is a relatively tricky and also murky topic in WebAssembly, however. There are two sets of instructions LLVM can emit for WebAssembly exceptions, Rust's Emscripten target supports exceptions, WASI targets do not, the LLVM flags to enable this are not always obvious, and additionally this all touches on "changing exception-handling behavior should be a target-level concern, not a feature". Effectively WebAssembly's exception-handling integration into Rust is not finalized at this time. The best idea at this time is that a parallel set of targets will eventually be added which support exceptions, but it's not clear if/when to do this. In the meantime the goal is to keep existing targets working while still enabling experimentation with exception-handling with `-Zbuild-std` and various permutations of LLVM flags.

To that extent this commit does not blanket disable these landing pads and cleanup routines for WebAssembly but instead checks to see if panic=unwind is enabled or if `+exception-handling` is enabled. Tests are updated here as well to account for this where, by default, using a `C-unwind` ABI won't affect Rust codegen at all. If `+exception-handling` is enabled, however, then Rust codegen will look like native platforms where exceptions are caught and the program aborts. More-or-less I've done my best to keep exceptions working on wasm where it's possible to have them work, but turned them off where they're not supposed to be emitted.

Closes rust-lang/rust#140293

pr.author: alexcrichton

issues.title: Exception handling instructions emitted on wasm even when exception-handling feature is disabled

analysis.originalLogic: Before the change, `AbortUnwindingCalls` computed `body_can_unwind` from the function's ABI and used it in two places: an `UnwindResume` terminator was rewritten to `UnwindTerminate(UnwindTerminateReason::Abi)` only `if !body_can_unwind`, and a call's cleanup was removed only `if !call_can_unwind`. The pass had no notion of whether the compilation target itself supports unwinding. The patch adds: `let target_supports_unwinding = !(tcx.sess.target.is_like_wasm && tcx.sess.panic_strategy() == PanicStrategy::Abort && !tcx.asm_target_features(def_id).contains(&sym::exception_handling));`
analysis.incorrectTransformation: On a wasm target with panic=abort and without the `exception-handling` target feature, the pre-fix pass still honored a call's `call_can_unwind` (e.g. calls through `C-unwind`/`extern "C-unwind"` ABIs) and kept its cleanup landing pad, and still rewrote `UnwindResume` only into `UnwindTerminate` rather than treating it as unreachable. That left invoke/landing-pad/unwind constructs in MIR on a target whose baseline cannot unwind, so LLVM either emitted exception-handling instructions (the issue reports `catch_call` is emitted) or hit an LLVM codegen/ICE-style error. The corrected behavior is: when `target_supports_unwinding` is false, rewrite `UnwindResume` to `TerminatorKind::Unreachable`, and enter the cleanup-removal branch via `if !call_can_unwind || !target_supports_unwinding`, turning the unwind action into `UnwindAction::Unreachable` instead of preserving a landing pad.
analysis.inputDomain: Functions compiled for a wasm target (issue uses wasm32-wasip1 or wasm32-unknown-unknown) with `-C panic=abort` and without `-Ctarget-feature=+exception-handling`, containing calls that the ABI says may unwind (notably `extern "C-unwind"` calls, e.g. `gzgetc` called from `gzgetc_`). The contrasting inputs are the same code on non-wasm targets, or on wasm with panic=unwind / `+exception-handling` enabled, where unwinding machinery is genuinely supported and must be retained. Inputs omit/reject features: `exception-handling` feature disabled is a precondition for the target to be treated as unable to unwind.
analysis.summary: `AbortUnwindingCalls` gained a `target_supports_unwinding` check so that wasm targets on panic=abort without `exception-handling` treat `UnwindResume` as `Unreachable` and suppress call cleanup landing pads even when the callee ABI is `C-unwind`, preventing LLVM from emitting unsupported EH instructions. Fixes rust-lang/rust#140293.
analysis.trigger: A call or `UnwindResume` in MIR whose ABI permits unwinding, on a target that fundamentally cannot unwind (wasm + PanicStrategy::Abort + no `exception-handling` target feature). The issue's reproducer is two `pub extern "C-unwind"` functions where one calls the other, built for wasm32 without `-Ctarget-feature=exception-handling`; `catch_call` appears at opt-level < 2.
preconditions: `asm_target_features(def_id)` does NOT contain `sym::exception_handling` (the `exception-handling` target feature is disabled).
The function body contains a call whose `call_can_unwind` is true (e.g. through a `C-unwind` ABI) or an `UnwindResume` terminator.
The pass must not have already returned early (e.g. due to panic strategy/AHB handling in the surrounding pass).
pitfalls: Do not blanket-disable landing pads/cleanup for all wasm: the fix checks panic=unwind and the `exception-handling` target feature so experimentation and Emscripten/WASI differences remain expressible.
Do not conflate `body_can_unwind` (function ABI) with `target_supports_unwinding` (target capability); the bug arose because only the former was consulted.
`UnwindResume` on a non-unwinding target must become `Unreachable`, not `UnwindTerminate`; the corrected branch tests `!target_supports_unwinding` before `!body_can_unwind`.
When `!call_can_unwind || !target_supports_unwinding`, the cleanup is replaced with `UnwindAction::Unreachable`; retaining the landing pad is the historically incorrect behavior.

A retained test name or old comment does not prove the fixed output; compare the actual revision-specific CHECK/NOT lines. The wasm default now expects `call` rather than `invoke` and no EH instructions.
analysis.testStrategy: Use codegen-llvm tests with explicit revisions rather than one expectation: `NONWASM` with `ignore-wasm32`, `WASM` with `only-wasm32` (default, no EH feature), and `WASMEXN` with `only-wasm32` plus `-Ctarget-feature=+exception-handling`. For default wasm assert absence of EH constructs: `WASM-NOT: call void @{{.*core9panicking19panic_cannot_unwind}}`, `WASM-NOT: invoke void @may_panic()`, `WASM-NOT: catchswitch`, `WASM-NOT: catchpad`, `WASM-NOT: catchret`, and presence of `WASM: call void @may_panic()`. For `WASMEXN` assert `invoke`, `cleanuppad`/`catchswitch`/`catchpad`/`catchret`, and the `__gxx_wasm_personality_v0` attribute, matching native behavior. Keep the non-wasm checks for the `panic_cannot_unwind` call. The WASMEXN intrinsic test uses the raw `llvm.wasm.throw` intrinsic via `link_llvm_intrinsics` because libstd's builtin was compiled with `-Cpanic=abort`, and is gated `#[cfg(wasmexn)]`.
